goal: Adopt an authentication state strategy for admin-panel so that sign-in works securely for the five-person internal team that uses it.
question: Select the authentication state strategy that best matches admin-panel as it exists today (internal five-person team, single-origin server-rendered app with no external API consumers, Python standard-library implementation, no auth logic yet), while remaining workable if the undecided mobile-app roadmap item is later pursued.
known_constraints: The app is an internal admin panel for a five-person team (README.md).
The app is server-rendered by its own web server and served from a single origin (README.md).
There are no external API consumers today (README.md).
The product roadmap mentions a possible mobile app, but nothing has been decided (README.md).
The implementation is stdlib-only Python on http.server; authentication is not implemented yet beyond a placeholder sign-in form (app.py).

environment.origin_model: single origin, no external API consumers
environment.auth_status: placeholder sign-in form only, no session or token logic implemented
environment.dependency_files: none (repository contains only app.py, README.md, and .claude/)

evidence: admin-panel is described as an internal admin panel for a five-person team (README.md).
The app is server-rendered by its own web server and served from a single origin (README.md).
There are no external API consumers today (README.md).
A possible mobile app appears on the product roadmap but nothing has been decided (README.md).
The server is minimal Python standard-library code using http.server, self-described as 'stdlib only' (app.py docstring and imports).
Authentication is not implemented yet; the page contains only a placeholder sign-in form (app.py PAGE constant).
The server currently binds to 127.0.0.1:8080 (app.py __main__ block).
No requirements.txt, package.json, or other dependency manifest exists in the repository (repository listing).

alternatives.name: Server-Side Session Cookie
alternatives.description: Issue a random opaque session ID in an HttpOnly cookie at sign-in and keep session state (user, expiry) in server-side storage such as process memory or a table.
advantages: The cookie carries only an opaque identifier, so no credential or claim data is exposed to the client.
The browser sends an HttpOnly cookie automatically on same-origin requests, which matches the current form-based, server-rendered flow.
Sessions can be expired or revoked immediately by deleting server-side state.
Can be implemented with the Python standard library (secrets, hmac, http.cookies) without adding dependencies.
disadvantages: Requires server-side session storage and cleanup of expired sessions.
Every request needs a session lookup, which couples the app to that state store if it is ever scaled horizontally.
A native mobile client would need a cookie-capable HTTP stack to reuse the same authentication.
assumptions: A single server process can hold session state for the five-person team.
Credentials are verified at sign-in and the app is served over TLS in production.

alternatives.name: Stateless JWT Bearer Token
alternatives.description: Issue a signed, self-contained JWT at sign-in and verify its signature and expiry on each request without any server-side session store.
advantages: No server-side session store is needed; each request is verified from the token itself.
The bearer-token model can be reused unchanged by native mobile or external API clients.
Standard claims such as exp carry expiry without any lookup.
disadvantages: Revoking a token before it expires requires an additional denylist, which reintroduces server-side state.
Signature verification and claim validation are more error-prone to hand-roll on the standard library, and a JWT library would add a dependency.
Token claims are readable by anyone who obtains the token unless it is also encrypted.
assumptions: A signing secret or key pair is configured outside the source tree.
Short token lifetimes, or a denylist for admin sessions, are acceptable.

alternatives.name: HTTP Basic Auth Per Request
alternatives.description: Have the browser send Base64-encoded credentials in an Authorization header on every request and verify them against the team member list, with no session or token state at all.
advantages: No session state, tokens, or cookies need to be created or stored.
The browser's built-in credential prompt avoids building and maintaining sign-in pages.
Requires only a small amount of standard-library code to decode and check the header.
disadvantages: Credentials are re-transmitted on every request, and there is no logout beyond closing the browser.
No built-in expiry, lockout, or per-session revocation, which limits lifecycle control for an admin panel.
Errors such as account lockout or rate limiting must be implemented from scratch.
assumptions: The app is always served over TLS so that repeated credential transmission is protected.
The five team members' credentials can be verified server-side with an appropriate password hash store.

criteria.name: Credential and session security
rubric: Credentials or session material are exposed to the client with no expiry or revocation path
Session material is protected and expires, but cannot be revoked before expiry
Session material is opaque, HttpOnly, expiring, and can be revoked immediately by the server

criteria.name: Fit with the current single-origin server-rendered app
rubric: Requires changing the app's architecture or adding a new client contract
Works for the same-origin browser flow but with notable friction
Natural fit for same-origin browser requests with no added client contract

criteria.name: Implementation simplicity with the standard library
rubric: Requires new dependencies or hand-rolled cryptographic verification
Feasible on the standard library but with a moderate amount of custom security code
A small amount of straightforward standard-library code

criteria.name: Flexibility if a mobile app is later added

Usable by a new client type after modest adaptation
Works unchanged for both browser and native clients
